name: Data Breach / Cyber Incident
description: Security incident response structure. Activates when a confirmed breach, ransomware, or unauthorized access is detected. Designed for rapid containment, evidence preservation, and regulatory compliance.
trigger_conditions: Confirmed breach detected by SOC (unauthorized access to systems or data)
Ransomware note received on any production or internal system
Data leaked on dark web — confirmed as organization data
Regulatory notification received regarding a suspected breach
Third-party vendor breach that may impact organizational data
Insider threat — confirmed data exfiltration by employee or contractor
Loss or theft of company-issued device containing sensitive data

responsibilities: Overall incident command and decision authority
Decide containment vs. investigation priority trade-offs
Resource allocation during response (personnel, budget, tools)
Approve external IR firm engagement
Declare incident resolved and authorize return to normal operations
Report to CEO and board on incident status
Technical containment — isolate affected systems, block IOCs
Evidence preservation — capture disk images, memory dumps, logs
System restoration coordination with IT/DevOps
Forensic investigation oversight (internal or external)
Track attacker TTPs and update detection rules
Maintain incident timeline and technical documentation
Regulatory notification (72-hour GDPR clock starts at detection)
Customer notification strategy and timing
Internal staff communications about the incident
Press statement preparation and approval
FAQ drafting for customers, partners, and press inquiries
Privilege management — ensure investigation runs under legal privilege
Law enforcement coordination (FBI, CISA, local authorities)
Liability assessment — contractual, regulatory, insurance
Data privacy compliance — GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, SOX determinations
Insurance carrier notification within policy timelines
Third-party vendor contractual notification obligations

key_actions: 1. Isolate affected systems immediately — preserve evidence (do not power off; isolate network)
2. Engage incident response retainer (CrowdStrike, Mandiant, SecureWorks, etc.)
3. Determine if PII/PCI/PHI was exposed — scope the breach
4. Notify insurance carrier within policy timeline (typically 24-48 hours)
5. Prepare regulatory notification (72hr GDPR, 30-day CCPA, HIPAA 60-day, state breach laws)
6. Engage external counsel for privilege protection if internal GC is insufficient
7. Develop customer communication plan with legal approval
8. Begin forensic investigation — root cause, scope, timeline
9. Implement containment and eradication — remove attacker access
10. Post-incident review within 2 weeks — lessons learned, control improvements

communication_protocol.internal: Crisis Lead sends daily update to board and CEO. Ops Lead sends hourly operational update to Crisis Lead during active containment. No technical details shared broadly — need-to-know basis only.
communication_protocol.external: All external communications must be approved by General Counsel. No technical staff authorized to speak to press, regulators, or law enforcement directly. Single designated spokesperson only.
communication_protocol.cadence: Standup every 2 hours during active response. Daily standup after containment is achieved. Weekly during remediation phase.

escalation_timeline.t0_30min: Detect → Initial Triage → Activate Crisis Command → Engage Ops Lead
escalation_timeline.t30min_4hr: Contain affected systems → Engage external counsel → Notify insurance carrier → Begin evidence preservation
escalation_timeline.t4_24hr: Forensic investigation → Determine breach scope → Identify exposed data types → Prepare regulatory notifications
escalation_timeline.t24_72hr: File regulatory notifications (GDPR: 72hr) → Prepare customer notification templates → Engage PR if public disclosure likely
escalation_timeline.t72hr_2wk: Deliver customer notifications → Remediation and eradication → Implement security improvements → Begin post-incident review
